newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop 1.56 pct on bank, property worry.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop 1.56 pct on bank, property worry.

text.p: Despite late local mutual fund buying, Thai stocks ended at a 39-month low on Monday after investors sold shares on worries over bank earnings and concern that some property firms may have cash problems, brokers said.

The SET index moved in negative zone throughout the session but trimmed losses slightly to end off 14.56 points at 918.30. It was the lowest close since July 28, 1993, when the index finished at 908.36. Total turnover was 2.9 billion baht.
"Foreigners continued to sell today. The mood wasn't good due to some talk that some property firms may be having cash problems," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.

Talk in the market today that some listed property companies may face cash problems came after rumours on Thursday that property developer Somprasong Land Plc was having cash problems and was in difficult position to settle its debt owed to some finance companies.
Somprasong Land, which slipped one baht to 10.25 today, has denied the rumours.
Analysts said investors were shunning the property developer's shares after the damaging rumours and also because its prospects for profit growth this year were small.

"Expectations of poor third quarter corporate results, due to be released later this month, also affected the market," Thanadech said. Anticipation of poor results in the banking sector, especially, triggered foreign selling, brokers said.

Krung Thai Bank, Thailand's second largest commercial bank, topped the active list in terms of value, down 5.50 baht to 75. National Finance and Securities slipped 2.75 to 47.75 and large capitalised TelecomAsia down 0.25 baht t0 49.50.
Brokers said the market is expected to fall slightly on Tuesday on the lack of positive news and foreigners are seen to be continued sellers. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
